rulings.restated:
Input — Any additional Form 1040 line 16 tax or filing, including any of the following?

A child's unearned income:
- filing Form 8814 (even with no tax)
- Form 8615, required if all of these apply:
  - you had more than $2,700 of unearned income
  - you are required to file
  - you do not file jointly
  - you have a parent who was alive at the end of 2025
  - you were under 18 at the end of 2025, or 18 with earned income of not more than half your support, or a full-time student 19 to 23 with earned income of not more than half your support

Foreign corporations:
- a section 962 election
- Form 8621
- stock you own, directly or indirectly, in a controlled foreign corporation (CFC) or a passive foreign investment company (PFIC), even with nothing to include in income for 2025 (its distributions, dispositions and related adjustments can make the modified AGI of Form 8960 line 13 differ from AGI)

Other:
- Form 4972
- a Form 8978 amount
- recapture of an education credit
- income averaging of farming or fishing income on Schedule J (if you choose it)
rulings.model: The restatement treats CFC/PFIC stock ownership as an additional Form 1040 line 16 tax/filing, but IRS i8960 says CFC/PFIC ownership may require MAGI adjustments on Form 8960 line 13: "If you own, directly or indirectly, stock in a CFC or PFIC ... to calculate your MAGI, you may need to make certain adjustments to your AGI" and "enter your AGI ... on line 13 of Form 8960."
rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i8960 p. 22: "If you exclude amounts under section 911 or own certain CFCs or PFICs, your MAGI is your AGI as modified by certain rules". As the prior ruling: CFC/PFIC ownership is in this refusal screen deliberately, with its reason stated, and the over-refusal of an owner with no NIIT was accepted. No amount is computed from the question. Project stands.

rulings.model: The restatement treats statutory-employee, minister, and church-employee income as Schedule 1 items, but the IRS text assigns them to Schedule SE: 'If you must pay SE tax, include this income on Schedule SE, line 2' and 'include on line 8a statutory employee social security wages and tips from Form W-2'.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040sse p. 1, Employees of Churches and Church Organizations; i1040gi p. 43, Clergy. The objection is that statutory-employee, clergy and church-employee income go to Schedule SE rather than Schedule 1. The question lists them expressly ("including ..."), so a filer with any of them answers Yes and the return is refused; the tool supports self-employment tax only for Schedule C income (person.se_screen refuses the same items). Whether each item also reaches Schedule 1 does not change who is refused. The person-dep wording (PENDING-5: "a church or qualified church-controlled organization") matches i1040sse p. 1. render MISMATCH. Project stands.

rulings.restated:
Input — Any income or adjustment requiring Schedule 1 other than the ones this tool asks about separately, including any of the following?

Income:
- statutory-employee wages or income as a minister, a member of a religious order who has not taken a vow of poverty, or a Christian Science practitioner
- church employee income (wages from a church or qualified church-controlled organization that elected exemption from social security and Medicare taxes)
- a refund or other recovery of an amount you deducted or took a credit for in an earlier year, other than a state or local income tax refund, for example:
  - a refund of general sales tax, real estate tax or personal property tax
  - a refund of mortgage interest in box 4 of Form 1098
  - a reimbursement of medical expenses
  - a payment on a bad debt you deducted
- sales of business property (Form 4797)
- a net operating loss deduction
- rental real estate, royalties, partnerships, S corporations, estates or trusts (Schedule E or a Schedule K-1)
- rental of personal property
- farm income (Schedule F)
- an exclusion of Medicaid waiver payments (Schedule 1 line 8s)

Adjustments:
- other qualified retirement plans for the self-employed (such as a solo 401(k) or other Keogh plan)
- an adjustment on Schedule 1 line 12, 14 or 23

The ones this tool asks about separately:
- business income or loss from Schedule C
- a taxable state or local income tax refund
- alimony under an agreement made before 2019
- unemployment compensation
- the line 8 items asked one by one
- educator expenses
- the HSA deduction
- the deductible part of self-employment tax
- self-employed SEP and SIMPLE contributions
- the self-employed health insurance deduction
- the penalty on early withdrawal of savings
- the IRA deduction
- student loan interest
- jury duty pay you gave your employer

Schedule 1-A deductions are asked separately.
rulings.model: The restatement lists statutory-employee, minister, and church-employee income as Schedule 1 items, but the IRS text directs statutory employee social security wages and tips to Schedule SE line 8a ("be sure to include on line 8a statutory employee social security wages and tips from Form W-2") and minister/church-employee income to Schedule SE lines 2/5a, not Schedule 1.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040sse p. 1. The question lists statutory-employee wages, income as a minister and church employee income so that a filer with them answers Yes and is refused; it does not say their amounts are entered on Schedule 1 (statutory employee income goes on Schedule C, whose net profit Schedule 1 line 3 carries, and clergy and church employee income bring Schedule SE, whose deduction is Schedule 1 line 15). The words are the prior wording's; the prior ruling on these items stands. Project stands.
